inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement, us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation = $136M (FY2024 $254M, FY2023 $188M). No PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation tag is filed, so no equity-award withholding is added; at 0.9% of revenue the omission is immaterial.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases $197M (FY2024 $235M). Zero in H1-2026: buybacks suspended under the merger agreement. Flat share count is a modelling convention, not currently funded.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: 28 December (52/53-week year ending the Sunday nearest 31 December)
inputs.share_count_basis: Q2-2026 10-Q weighted-average diluted shares 1,923M (basic 1,920M; cover-page basic 1,920.8M at 2026-07-31). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. No non-SBC issuance is expected; the merger converts every share into consideration rather than issuing new Kenvue stock.
inputs.net_debt_note: Q2-2026 10-Q us-gaap:DebtLongtermAndShorttermCombinedAmount $8,480M = $7,074M senior notes (after the $750M March-2026 maturity was repaid, refinanced with commercial paper) + $1,406M commercial paper and other short-term borrowings; cash $1,110M. The Metrics CSV / DB TotalDebt column (1,406) is the DebtCurrent tag only and understates debt by ~$7.1B; FY2023's 8,286 was the correct combined figure. Fair value of the notes is $6.8B, i.e. below carrying value because coupons are below the current 5.2% ten-year.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. Risk-free 5.24% = 10-year UST close 2026-09-28 (^TNX; 5-day closes 4.97-5.24, 5-year at 5.07). ERP 4.5%, beta 0.65 (consumer-health staple, low cyclicality) -> cost of equity 8.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt 5.4% (FY2025 10-K short-term weighted-average rate; notes indicated ~5-5.5%), 27% tax -> 3.9% after tax. Market-value weights: equity $34.4B (1,923M x 17.88), debt $8.5B -> D/V 20% -> WACC 7.35%, rounded UP to 7.5% for the rate volatility of the last week. One WACC across all three scenarios; scenario risk is carried by the driver paths and the probability weights, never by per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A: operating-lease rent stays inside EBITDA (US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases are an opex line), so the $133M of operating lease liabilities at Q2-2026 are NOT added to net debt. No finance leases of consequence.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. Kenvue has no material non-controlling interests (no MinorityInterest tag filed); all flows are attributable.
inputs.interest_treatment: Reported FCF ($1,722M FY2025) is AFTER $440M of interest paid, i.e. levered. The component build below is unlevered (EBITDA -> EBIT -> NOPAT), so interest never enters the projected flows and net debt is deducted once from EV. The unlevered equivalent of FY2025 reported FCF is ~$2,040M (1,722 + 440 x (1 - 0.27)); the year-1 owner-FCF sanity check is against that figure, not against the levered $1,586M. Interest income of $51M (InterestIncomeOther) is not deducted: net debt, not net cash.
inputs.notes: MODEL: standalone owner-FCF component DCF (engine route) used as the DEAL-BREAKS leg of a deal-completes vs deal-breaks framing, per the dcf-methods routing row for a live takeover. Kenvue is under a signed, shareholder-approved (2026-01-29), HSR-cleared (2026-02-04) acquisition by Kimberly-Clark for $3.50 cash + 0.14625 KMB shares per KVUE share, expected to close Q4 2026; K-C launched exchange offers for Kenvue's notes on 2026-09-28 conditioned on completion. Kenvue has withdrawn all guidance. The three scenarios here value Kenvue as an independent company -- what a holder surrenders in exchange for the consideration, and what the stock reverts to if the deal breaks. They deliberately EXCLUDE K-C's $2.1B synergy target, which accrues to the combined entity through the KMB shares, not to Kenvue standalone. The consideration arithmetic, close probability and deal-weighted expected value are in the `deal_overlay` block; `probability_weighted.weighted_iv` is the standalone (deal-breaks) value and must be read alongside it. Base revenue is FY2025 (fiscal year ended 2025-12-28); year 1 is FY2026, of which H1 is reported (+3.7% reported, +1.6% organic in Q2, GAAP EBITDA margin 22.3% vs 20.2% in H1-2025). TTM to Q2-2026: revenue $15,408M, GAAP EBITDA $3,197M (20.7%), reported FCF $1,914M.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Category growth: global consumer-health / OTC grows low-to-mid single digits; Kenvue's Q2-2026 organic +1.6% after -2.2% in FY2025. Historical CAGRs are unusable as a forward anchor (see notes).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-18.6%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (+0.4%) because the 2023 separation from J&J stripped ~$9B of equity (debt-funded distribution to J&J plus the buyback of J&J's stake). EPS CAGR (-13.7%) carries separation, stand-up and restructuring charges plus post-spin interest on $8B of new debt. Neither describes the operating business.
historical_growth.notes: Only five fiscal years exist (FY2021-FY2025), so 5-year CAGRs cannot be computed; 4-year figures are given instead. FY2021-FY2022 are carve-out financials prepared for the IPO: FY2021 OCF of $334M / FCF of $39M reflects J&J's cash management, not Kenvue's, so the owner-FCF CAGR is measured from FY2022. Owner FCF series (reported FCF less SBC): FY2022 2,013; FY2023 2,511; FY2024 1,081 (talc/separation cash costs, working-capital build); FY2025 1,586; TTM Q2-2026 ~1,853. SBC-adjusted 3-yr FCF CAGR (-7.6%) is below the reported CAGR (-7.2%) only marginally: SBC is small and shrank in FY2025 as post-spin founder grants vested. Revenue has been flat for four years; the forward anchor is category growth, not history.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +2.5% (H1 reported +3.7% with FX tailwind, organic +1.6%; H2 comps harder and the Tylenol-autism headline hit volumes from late Sept 2025). FY2027 +2.0% while a new permanent CEO resets the portfolio; then 2.5% = category growth with no share gain.
base.margin_note: GAAP EBITDA margin FY2025 19.6% (after $290M restructuring), H1-2026 22.3%, TTM 20.7%. Base ramps 21% -> 23% as separation/stand-up costs roll off and the Vue Forward program lands; 23% is below Kenvue's adjusted ~24% and below Haleon (~24%) because recurring restructuring is treated as a real cost, not added back.
base.tax_note: FY2025 cash taxes $595M on pretax $1,999M = 29.8% (timing); GAAP ETR 26.5% FY2025, 26.8% H1-2026. Path 27.5% -> 27% applied to unlevered EBIT.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer/distributor: receivables + inventory exceed payables (net operating WC ~11% of revenue), so growth consumes cash; capture -10% of the revenue change.
base.cap_note: 18x terminal FCF (Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% would give 20.5x): a mature staples exit multiple; K-C is paying ~14.8x EBITDA / ~24x unlevered FCF, which includes control synergies a standalone holder does not get.

bull.narrative: Standalone self-help works: Starboard-driven cost discipline and a permanent CEO lift EBITDA margin to 25% (Haleon-plus), Skin Health returns to growth on Neutrogena/Aveeno innovation and Asia-Pacific/LatAm, e-commerce mix improves, and the Tylenol litigation is dismissed again on remand. 3-3.5% growth is share gain over category; 20x cap is a full staples multiple.

bear.narrative: The deal breaks and Kenvue is left with the FY2025 problem set plus a live mass tort: the revived (July 2026) acetaminophen-autism cases proceed to trial, an FDA pregnancy label change lands, Tylenol volumes fall and defense/settlement costs sit permanently inside a 19.5% EBITDA margin (~1.5pp below FY2026 run-rate). Private label keeps taking share in allergy, pain and skin care; organic growth stalls at 0-1.5%. No margin recovery, 15x cap. Litigation is charged through margin and growth rather than as a separate reserve because no reasonable estimate has been disclosed.

scenario_narratives.base: Kenvue as an independent consumer-health company after a deal break, run competently but without K-C's synergies: category-rate growth of ~2.5% (FY2025 organic -2.2% was the trough; Q2-2026 organic +1.6%), EBITDA margin recovering from the 19.6% GAAP FY2025 level to 23% as one-time separation and stand-up costs roll off, SBC ~0.8% of revenue, capex ~3%, cash tax 27%, and an 18x terminal FCF cap. The Tylenol litigation remains an unquantified overhang that is handled through the bear weight rather than the base flows.
scenario_narratives.bull: Self-help under activist pressure: margins to 25%, growth above category via Skin Health and international, litigation resolved without label change, 20x exit. This is roughly what K-C is paying for before synergies.
scenario_narratives.bear: Deal breaks into a live mass tort and a leadership vacuum: flat revenue, 19.5% margin with litigation costs inside it, 15x exit. Value falls to about half the consideration.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: These weight the STANDALONE distribution, i.e. the deal-breaks world (see deal_overlay for the deal-completes weighting). Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the acetaminophen-autism litigation was revived by the Second Circuit in July 2026 with 500+ cases, an interim CEO has run the company since July 2025, and organic sales fell across all three segments in FY2025. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: the bull case needs a new CEO, a margin program and a litigation win to all land, and none is in evidence yet. Base 50%.

deal_overlay.consideration_note: 3.50 + 0.14625 x 98.77 = 17.95. The headline $21.01 was struck on KMB ~119.7; KMB's ~17% fall since has cut the value of the stock leg by ~$3.06. No collar: KVUE holders bear KMB price risk through close.
deal_overlay.spread_note: 17.95 / 17.88 - 1 = +0.4%, plus one more quarterly KVUE dividend ($0.2075) if the record date precedes close. Roughly 2-3% annualised over ~3 months: the market is pricing completion as near-certain.
deal_overlay.status: Signed 2025-11; both shareholder votes passed 2026-01-29; HSR waiting period expired 2026-02-04; remaining conditions are customary foreign clearances; K-C commenced exchange offers / consent solicitations for Kenvue's notes on 2026-09-28, conditioned on completion; expected close Q4 2026.
deal_overlay.probability_note: All shareholder and US antitrust conditions are satisfied and the acquirer is executing its debt integration; residual risk is a foreign-clearance delay, a K-C financing/market shock, or a litigation development large enough to trigger an MAE dispute. 8% break probability is a judgment, not a market-implied figure (the spread is too thin to back one out).
deal_overlay.deal_weighted_value_formula: p_close x consideration_value_now + (1 - p_close) x probability_weighted.weighted_iv (standalone)
deal_overlay.deal_weighted_value_note: Compute from the generated JSON: 0.92 x 17.95 + 0.08 x weighted_iv. With standalone weighted IV in the mid-teens this lands within a few cents of the current price. The economically meaningful question for a holder is not 'is Kenvue cheap' but 'do I want 0.14625 KMB shares plus $3.50': the position is a KMB position with a small cash kicker after Q4 2026.
deal_overlay.synergies_excluded: K-C targets $2.1B run-rate synergies ($1.9B cost, $0.5B revenue) for the combined company. None is in the standalone scenarios; a KVUE holder's share of them is the KMB stock leg, valued at market.

entry_price.method_note: Hurdle entry prices are for the STANDALONE scenarios. A 15% IRR through the deal is not available: the consideration is ~$17.95 in ~3 months against a $17.88 price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Kenvue is in the last quarter of a signed, approved, HSR-cleared sale to Kimberly-Clark, so its market price is the value of $3.50 plus 0.14625 KMB shares, not a view on Kenvue's fundamentals. The dcf-methods routing sends a live takeover to deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting rather than three growth scenarios; this file does that by building the three scenarios as the STANDALONE company (the deal-breaks leg, and the asset a holder is surrendering) and carrying the deal leg in deal_overlay. The standalone base case values Kenvue below the consideration: flat revenue for four years, a GAAP EBITDA margin still ~3pp below its adjusted level, $7.4B of net debt refinanced into a 5.2% ten-year, and a revived mass tort. That gap is the answer to whether K-C's offer is adequate on a no-synergy basis: it is. Kenvue's FY2021-FY2025 history is largely non-informative for a forward view (carve-out years, separation charges, spin-related equity stripping) and the company has withdrawn guidance, so the drivers are anchored to H1-2026 run-rates and category growth.
key_risks_to_valuation: Deal break: a foreign regulatory delay, K-C financing shock or MAE claim around the acetaminophen litigation would drop the stock toward the standalone weighted IV, which is below the consideration.
KMB price: with no collar, every $1 move in KMB moves the consideration by $0.146; the stock leg is 80% of the package.

Acetaminophen-autism litigation (500+ cases revived July 2026; FDA citizen petition on pregnancy labelling): no disclosed loss estimate; charged through the bear weight and bear margin, not as a reserve.
Organic growth: all three segments declined in FY2025; base assumes only category-rate recovery, but private-label share loss could persist.

Debt anchor: the Metrics CSV TotalDebt column understates debt by ~$7.1B (DebtCurrent tag only); this valuation uses the combined-debt tag ($8,480M). Any downstream consumer reading the CSV column will overstate equity value by ~$3.7/share.
Rates: the 10-year moved ~27bp in the week before this valuation; WACC 7.5% is built on 5.24% and each 50bp on WACC moves the base value by roughly 8-10%.
